 O R D E R
1. The petitioners are the close family members of proforma respondent No.3, who is the husband of the complainant-respondent No.1 in T.P.(Crl.) No.467 of 2024.
2. The marriage between respondent No.1 and proforma respondent No.3 was solemnized on 04.11.2019.
She is alleged to have been thrown out of her matrimonial home on 22.04.2021 after she was assaulted.

Respondent No.1 has filed Complaint Case No.11352 of 2023, under Section 12 read with Sections 18, 19, 20 16:45:47 IST Reason:
and 22 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Family Court, North West, Rohini, New Delhi.

The petitioners seek transfer of Complaint Case No.11352/2023, titled Smt. Sana @ Samaya vs.
Mohd. Danish & Ors., filed by respondent No.1 under Section 12 read with Sections 18, 19, 20 and 22 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, pending before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Family Court, North West, Rohini, New Delhi to the Court of Judicial Magistrate, Hathras, U.P. and Criminal Case No.3384 of 2024, titled as State vs. Danish & Ors.,
filed under Sections 406, 34 and 498A IPC arising out of FIR No.548 of 2023, filed in PS Bharat Nagar, North West Delhi, pending before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, North West, Rohini,
New Delhi to the Court of Judicial Magistrate, Hathras, Uttar Pradesh.

sentences.text: 4. Vide order dated 20.05.2024, notice on the Transfer Petition was issued for the limited purpose to explore the possibility of a settlement between the parties.
Respondent No.1 has not entered appearance despite service.
We are informed that some criminal cases have been filed against respondent No.1 by her husband at Hathras, Uttar Pradesh.

5. Having heard learned counsel for the petitioners as well as learned Additional Solicitor General of India for the State of NCT of Delhi in T.P.(Crl.)No.560/2024, we are satisfied that no case to transfer the Complaint Case and the Criminal Case is made out.
6. The Transfer Petitions are, accordingly, dismissed.

However, those of the petitioners, who are senior citizens and/or home makers may seek their exemption from personal appearance, and an appropriate order shall be passed by the Metropolitan Magistrate on sympathetic consideration of such a prayer.
7. As a result, the pending interlocutory applications also stand disposed of.
